source.title: Capturing Polysemanticity with PRISM: A Multi-Concept Feature Description Framework
source.authors: Laura Kopf; Nils Feldhus; Kirill Bykov; P. Bommer; Anna Hedstrom; M. Höhne; Oliver Eberle

record.tranche_reason: Applies a multi-concept feature-description analysis to LLM neurons and SAE features, and reports polysemanticity results in those models. It does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The study measures semantic similarity among descriptions of a feature and includes human ratings for selected features. Benchmark AUROC and MAD results assess description quality, not superposition geometry, so they are not recorded as rows. The paper's citations and background discussion of capacity are not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces and benchmarks a feature-description method, PRISM. Its 'polysemanticity score' is the cosine similarity among LLM-written descriptions of activation clusters. That is a description-diversity construct, not a measure of superposition, capacity allocation, feature distribution across neurons, or SAE recovery. The human study validates PRISM's own score on 8 hand-picked features. No result bears directly on V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but misses the main point. The authors chiefly conclude that PRISM's multi-concept descriptions beat single-description methods on AUROC/MAD, and that its polysemanticity score aligns with human judgments. They add that polysemanticity varies across models and feature types with no consistent layer trend.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation-based sampling, clustering, LLM labeling, embedding similarity, and human ratings to study LLM features; it does not use the original toy-model superposition setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported polysemanticity varies across models and feature types; the paper reports no consistent trend across layer depth. Gemma Scope SAE descriptions are described as the most monosemantic across layers, while Llama 3.1 8B Instruct descriptions often approach the randomized similarity baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: PRISM description-similarity scores vary by model and show no consistent layer trend. Gemma Scope SAE features are the most monosemantic. Llama 3.1 8B Instruct MLP neuron descriptions often approach the random-description baseline. GPT-2 XL neuron 3815, layer 47, previously called 'possibly monosemantic', gets diverse descriptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons and SAE latents in LLMs respond to semantically heterogeneous inputs, as measured by diversity of automated descriptions, to a degree that varies by model and feature type.

record.problems: The human evaluation covers 8 features and 7 participants. The authors note that a fixed number of clusters cannot guarantee that all or the most salient concepts are captured, descriptions are limited to natural-language-expressible concepts, and sampling highly activating corpus examples can miss rare or out-of-distribution patterns. Polysemanticity is estimated from description similarity rather than a direct measurement of representational geometry.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant quantitative rows. Figure 3 reports layer-wise polysemanticity scores graphically and describes model-level trends in the text, but does not state the individual plotted values; the paper's AUROC/MAD benchmark tables measure description quality rather than the claim's representation geometry.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity-vs-dimension manipulation, phase transition or geometry.
No test of capacity or feature importance as the cause of polysemanticity.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not measure features spread across neurons or the quality of SAE recovery. It only measures diversity of descriptions for selected neurons and SAE latents.
No test of SAE feature completeness, stability or canonicality.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is a method and benchmark paper. Toy Models of Superposition is cited only as background on polysemanticity. The human study (7 participants, 8 features) is metric validation on hand-selected examples. Its values are selection values, not prevalence estimates, so no verdict labels are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature sparsity relative to dimensions, overlapping directions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether limited capacity causes polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Measures semantic diversity of feature descriptions but does not test whether it arises without capacity pressure or establish an alternative cause.
Tests semantic diversity of selected LLM features, including SAE features; does not test features being distributed across many neurons or measure SAE recovery of the model's features.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units, although it measures semantic diversity for some SAE features.
Does not test whether the underlying superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Small
rows.operation_detail: Compared human-rated similarity of five cluster descriptions for a feature with the PRISM polysemanticity score.
rows.measure: Human polysemanticity rating; PRISM description cosine-similarity score
rows.note: Lower scores indicate greater semantic diversity. The authors describe this feature as semantically diverse.
rows.check: This is a validation value for the study's own metric (human rating vs PRISM score) on a hand-selected feature. It is not a measure of superposition or SAE recovery. Layer 5, feature 30319 is correct.

rows.subject: Gemma Scope
rows.operation_detail: Human-rated similarity of five cluster descriptions for a feature.
rows.note: The paper describes high scores as indicating more consistent, monosemantic labeling.
rows.check: Method-validation value on a hand-selected feature. The subject should be a Gemma 2 residual-stream SAE (Gemma Scope), layer 0. The row omits the layer and the Human Cosine Similarity of 0.79. 'Absent' is not meaningful against any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The feature received low human and PRISM similarity scores, which the authors interpret as semantic diversity (p1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: These selected features received high human similarity ratings, consistent with relatively monosemantic descriptions rather than uniform polysemanticity (p2–p3).
